title: Implement a trie supporting inserting a word, searching for a complete word, and checking whether any word starts with a given prefix.
shortTitle: Implement a Trie (Prefix Tree) with Insert, Search, and startsWith

s1_definition.oneliner: A trie stores characters on edges so every path from root spells a prefix, and all operations cost only the key length.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Trie (prefix tree)** – a tree where each edge represents a character and each root-to-node path spells a prefix.
- **Node structure** – each node holds child links (map or array) and a boolean `isWord` marking end of a stored word.
- **Insert** – walk character by character, create missing children, set `isWord` on the final node.
- **Search** – walk character by character; succeed only if every character has a child and the final node has `isWord = true`.
- **startsWith** – walk character by character; succeed as long as every character has a child, ignoring `isWord`.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India stores customer reference codes in a branching filing system. You follow one letter at a time, creating a new drawer when one is missing. A flag in the final drawer marks a complete code. To check a code you follow the letters; missing drawers mean the code was never filed. To check a prefix you follow letters and stop, flag or not.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Trie Structure after inserting "NBI2024A", "NBI2024B", "HDFC001"

              [root]
             /       \
           N          H
           |          |
           B          D
           |          |
           I          F
           |          |
           2          C
           |          |
           0          0
           |          |
           2          0
           |          |
           4          1*
          / \
         A*  B*

  * = isWord = true

  Operations:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ insert("NBI2024A"):                         │
  │   Walk N->B->I->2->0->2->4->A              │
  │   Create missing nodes, set A.isWord=true   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ search("NBI"):                              │
  │   Walk N->B->I -> found node, isWord=false  │
  │   Return FALSE                              │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ startsWith("NBI"):                          │
  │   Walk N->B->I -> found node                │
  │   Return TRUE (isWord irrelevant)           │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A trie is a tree where each edge carries one character and each path from root spells a prefix. Words sharing a prefix share the same initial path, which saves space. Every node holds links to its children and a boolean marking whether a complete word ends there. Insert, search, and prefix checks all run in time proportional to the key length, independent of how many keys are stored.

The critical distinction between search and startsWith is one line of code: search checks the isWord flag on the final node, while startsWith only checks that the path exists. This is the most common bug in trie implementations: treating a prefix as a complete word.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used a trie to store registered reference codes for an internal staff console with prefix autocomplete. A HashSet could confirm an exact code but could not answer "does any code start with these characters" without scanning every entry. The trie answered prefix queries in time proportional to the prefix length.

The senior insight is when to use a trie versus a HashSet. Tries win for prefix queries, autocomplete, and ordered iteration. HashSets win for pure exact-match lookups with lower memory. In production, a radix tree compresses single-child chains to reduce per-node overhead, and the choice between array children and map children depends on alphabet size.

Remember one sentence: A trie stores characters on edges, the isWord flag distinguishes a complete word from a prefix, and all operations cost only the key length.

---

keyPoints: Each edge is a character; each root-to-node path spells a prefix.
The isWord flag distinguishes a complete word from a mere prefix.
Insert, search, and startsWith all run in O(key length) time.
Tries beat HashSets for prefix queries but use more memory per entry.
Compressed tries (radix trees) merge single-child chains to save space.
Trie powers autocomplete, spell checking, IP routing, and dictionary lookup.
